deviation: The draft refers to "a DPA" rather than the Arcadia DPA, and it doesn't bar processing until the DPA is signed ("executed, or will execute alongside"). It also drops the express duty to comply with applicable data protection law. This could let the Supplier process data under its own DPA terms or before any DPA is in place. The 24-hour breach notice and the export and deletion terms favour Arcadia.
suggested_text: 6.1 The Services involve the processing of Personal Data of the Customer's customers and employees. The Supplier shall process Personal Data only on the Customer's documented instructions and in accordance with applicable data protection law. The Parties shall execute the Customer's Data Processing Agreement (the "DPA") before any Personal Data is processed and in any event before go-live, and the DPA forms part of this Agreement. The Supplier shall not process any Personal Data until the DPA has been executed. 6.2 [retain draft 6.2 unchanged.] 6.3 [retain draft 6.3 unchanged.]
